mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same period are not statistically lower than during a similar pre-tightening period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer confidence (implied via HOUST) creates a dual-stress scenario that depresses equity risk premia, yielding negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases while HOUST decreases over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when the same labor indicators are not in decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% month-over-month suggests excess demand, which typically precedes equity market overvaluation and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > +2% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or flat despite INDPRO exceeding the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the RSAFS index (raw materials availability) of more than 10% over three months indicates tightening supply chains, which raises input costs and reduces corporate profit expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >10% over the past three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of stable supply conditions (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% while FEDFUNDS remains above 4%, the dual signal of weak labor and persistent monetary tightening is interpreted as a deflationary environment that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive or the combination of indicators is not detected in the data (e.g., UNRATE never below 4% in the sample).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in PAYEMS (labor market activity) by more than 5% in a month suggests wage growth acceleration, which can trigger equity market optimism and produce positive 20-day forward returns when combined with a falling CPIAUCSL (inflation pressure).
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% while CPIAUCSL decreases over the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive when the wage and inflation signals are not in the specified direction.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL < 305 over 3 months) without a corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a cooling demand environment, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 305 for three consecutive months and INDPRO flat or declining
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when demand is cooling but production is rising.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 3% for four consecutive months in a low-unemployment regime (PAYEMS < 50K), the signal of accommodative policy is persistent and tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% for four consecutive months and PAYEMS < 50K
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when policy is not persistently accommodative or unemployment is high.
